title: Metric-bound rollback orchestration for config sweeps with adaptive sample sizing
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: We frequently run configuration and model sweeps that introduce subtle quality regressions only visible at small traffic fractions. Current canary/A-B gates either take too long (fixed sample sizes) or trigger noisy rollbacks (naive thresholds), which both increase time-to-safe-deploy and developer friction.

Objective: Build an observability-first, metric-bound rollback orchestrator that: 1) automatically detects statistically-meaningful degradation across multiple quality slices, 2) adapts sample sizing to reach decisions faster for high-signal metrics and slower for noisy signals, and 3) triggers automated rollback or traffic adjustments with explainable provenance.

Scope: This ticket implements the controller and experiment logic (traffic allocation, sequential tests, alarm plumbing, rollback actions) for config/model change rollouts in the staging and production rollout pipelines. It excludes UI work (Console dashboards) and dedicated capacity autoscaler integration, which will be separate follow-ups.

Design highlights: 1) Multi-metric guard: Support a configurable set of primary and secondary metrics (e.g., end-to-end BLEU/ROUGE surrogate scores, hallucination-rate, latency P95, token-error-rate, per-customer conversion). Each metric has: direction (increase/decrease bad), minimum detectable effect (MDE), and weighting for composite decision. 2) Sequential testing engine: Use an SPRT (Sequential Probability Ratio Test) core with configurable alpha/beta spend per metric, fallback to Bayesian credible intervals for very low-throughput cohorts. 3) Adaptive sample sizing: Monitor instantaneous signal-to-noise; if variance is low, shrink required sample and make earlier decisions. If noisy, extend sampling window automatically up to a safe cap. 4) Cohort slicing & provenance: Evaluate by cohort (customer, region, model-config), persist evaluation snapshots and seed hashes so decisions are reproducible and auditable. 5) Explainable rollback actions: Rollback records include list of top contributing metrics, effect sizes, and the test statistic; orchestration emits a causal trace linking request IDs, rollout id, and regression evidence. 6) Safety overrides: Manual hold, dry-run-only mode, and a throttled auto-rollback (max one rollback per 24h per project) to reduce oscillation.

Implementation plan: Phase 1 (this ticket): Build the testing engine and controller, integrate with existing traffic router to dynamically shift traffic fractions, emit evaluation events to observability bus, and implement a simple policy (any primary metric crossing configured threshold with p<0.01 triggers rollback) for prod-staged rollouts. Phase 2: Add composite decision function (weighted scoring), integrate Console decision view, and add config-driven sample caps. Phase 3: Extend to Dedicated/private deployments with local telemetry ingest.

Telemetry sources: eval-runner scores (batch), streaming request traces (per-token latency), KV cache hit-rate, and error logs. We'll normalize metrics into a common units pipeline and attach sample weights.

Trade-offs considered: - Strict thresholds reduce customer regressions but can cause false rollbacks for noisy signals. We use adaptive sampling + sequential tests to minimize both. - SPRT is efficient but requires model assumptions; we provide Bayesian fallback and conservative defaults. - Automated rollback reduces MTTR but increases risk of oscillation; we enforce cooldowns and human overrides.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for SPRT/Bayesian core, integration tests with a traffic router simulator, synthetic regressions injected via the eval harness, and a staged rollout to internal canary tenants (10% traffic) before enabling full auto-rollback in production.

Deliverables: controller service, sequential-test library, migration guide for existing rollouts, telemetry schema, and PR with feature flag gating.
acceptance_criteria: Sequential testing library implemented with SPRT and Bayesian fallback and covered by unit tests
Controller can allocate traffic (1%, 5%, 10%, 25%) and run continuous evaluations against configured metrics
Automated rollback action created that reverts model/config and records provenance to audit log
Dashboard event stream and evaluation snapshots emitted to observability bus (events include rollout_id, metric, effect_size, p_value)
Cooldown and manual override controls implemented and feature-flagged
